gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the past continuous of the verb in brackets (was/were + -ing). In negatives use wasn’t/weren’t; in questions include the subject. Twenty original sentences.

questions.before: At nine o’clock last night, Grandpa
questions.after: the dishes.
questions.explain: An action in progress at a specific past time: nine o’clock last night.

questions.after: on the beach.
questions.explain: -ie → -ying: lie → lying. ‘We’ takes ‘were’.

questions.before: At half past seven this morning, Ben
questions.after: for the school bus.
questions.explain: An action in progress at a specific past time. ‘Ben’ (he) takes ‘was’.

questions.before: At midnight last night, the neighbours
questions.after: a party.
questions.explain: Drop the -e before -ing: have → having. ‘The neighbours’ (they) takes ‘were’.

questions.after: breakfast when the postman knocked on the door.
questions.explain: Breakfast was in progress when the postman knocked. Drop the -e: have → having.

questions.after: her bike when she saw the accident.
questions.explain: The longer action in progress takes the past continuous. Drop the -e: ride → riding.

questions.after: football when it started to rain.
questions.explain: The football was in progress when the rain started.

questions.after: in the park when he met his old teacher.
questions.explain: Double the final consonant: jog → jogging.

questions.use: Two actions at the same time
questions.after: dinner, I was doing my homework.
questions.explain: Two actions in progress at the same time: both take the past continuous.

questions.after: TV, the power went out.
questions.explain: The TV was in progress when the power went out. ‘We’ takes ‘were’.

questions.use: Two actions at the same time
questions.after: a book while his sister was painting.
questions.explain: Two actions at the same time: both are past continuous.

questions.use: Two actions at the same time
questions.after: around the garden while their parents were talking.
questions.explain: Double the final consonant: run → running.

questions.before: When you called at nine last night, I
questions.after: TV — I was reading in bed.
questions.explain: When you called, the TV wasn’t on: the action wasn’t in progress at that moment. Negative past continuous: wasn’t + -ing.

questions.after: when the teacher came in. They were chatting.
questions.explain: Negative past continuous: ‘they’ takes weren’t + -ing.

questions.after: her seat belt when the car stopped suddenly.
questions.explain: Negative past continuous: ‘she’ takes wasn’t + -ing.

questions.before: When the teacher gave the instructions, we
questions.after: attention — we were looking out of the window.
questions.explain: When the teacher spoke, the action wasn’t in progress: we were doing something else. ‘We’ takes weren’t + -ing.

questions.after: at ten o’clock last night?
questions.explain: Questions put was/were first: Were you sleeping…?

questions.after: when I phoned you?
questions.explain: In a wh- question, was/were comes right after the question word: What were you doing…?

questions.after: in the rain at six o’clock yesterday?
questions.explain: In a wh- question, was/were comes right after the question word.

questions.after: dinner when the storm started?
questions.explain: Questions put was/were first: Was she cooking…?

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples covering past moments, interrupted actions, negatives and questions.

sentences.use: Two actions at the same time
Two actions at the same time

matching.title: Match the -ing form
matching.subtitle: Tap a base verb, then tap its -ing form. Watch the spelling: some drop an -e, some double a letter.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Check the time clue (when, while, at eight o’clock) and watch for state verbs.

questions.text: At eight o’clock last night, I        TV and my brother was doing his homework.
wrongReasons: ‘Watched’ is past simple. At eight o’clock last night the action was in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘am watching’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘I’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
questions.explain: An action in progress at a specific past time (eight o’clock last night) takes the past continuous.

questions.text: I was having a shower when the phone       .
wrongReasons: The short action that interrupts takes the past simple: ‘rang’, not ‘was ringing’.
Wrong tense: ‘rings’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Had rung’ is past perfect: it would mean the phone rang before the shower.
questions.explain: The short action that interrupts the longer one is past simple: rang.

questions.text: At three o’clock yesterday afternoon, she        a book and the baby was sleeping.
wrongReasons: ‘Read’ is past simple. At three o’clock the action was in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘is reading’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘she’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
questions.explain: An action in progress at a specific past time (three o’clock yesterday afternoon) takes the past continuous.

questions.text: The students were writing when the fire alarm       .
wrongReasons: The short action that interrupts takes the past simple: ‘went off’.
Wrong tense: ‘goes off’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Had gone off’ is past perfect: it would mean the alarm sounded before they wrote.
questions.explain: The short action that interrupts is past simple: went off.

questions.text: He        a new bike, so he saved money all year.
wrongReasons: ‘Want’ is a state verb, so it doesn’t take the continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘wants’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Has wanted’ is present perfect. The story is finished: ‘wanted’.
questions.explain: State verbs like want, know and like use the past simple.

questions.text: The twins        arguing when Mum walked in.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘the twins’ (they) takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘Have been’ + -ing is present perfect continuous, but ‘when Mum walked in’ is a finished past time: ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘are’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: ‘The twins’ = they, so use ‘were’ + -ing.

questions.text: you sleeping when I called last night?
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘you’ takes ‘Were’, not ‘Was’.
‘Is’ is present and goes with he/she/it. Here it’s past and the subject is ‘you’: ‘Were’.
Wrong tense: ‘Are’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: ‘You’ takes ‘were’. Questions put was/were first.

questions.text: When I looked out of the window, Dad        the car and Mum was packing the bags.
wrongReasons: ‘Washed’ is past simple. When I looked out, the washing was already in progress: ‘was washing’.
Wrong tense: ‘is washing’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘Dad’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
questions.explain: When I looked out, the washing was already in progress.

questions.text: He was running for the bus when he        his phone.
wrongReasons: The short action that interrupts takes the past simple: ‘dropped’.
Wrong tense: ‘drops’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Had dropped’ is past perfect: it would mean he dropped it before running.
questions.explain: The short action that interrupts is past simple: dropped.

questions.text: At seven this morning, I was brushing my teeth and my sister        breakfast.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘made’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘is making’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘my sister’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
questions.explain: Two actions in progress at the same past time are both past continuous.

questions.text: What        you doing when the lights went out?
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘you’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘Is’ is present and goes with he/she/it. ‘You’ in the past takes ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘are’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: ‘You’ takes ‘were’. In a wh- question, was/were comes right after the question word.

questions.text: She        in the garden when she heard a strange noise.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘she’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘worked’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘is working’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: The long action in progress is past continuous; ‘heard’ is the short action that interrupts.

questions.text: They        football in the park when it started to snow, so they stopped the match.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘played’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘are playing’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘they’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
questions.explain: The match was in progress when the snow started.

questions.text: I        that you were busy, so I didn’t call.
wrongReasons: ‘Know’ is a state verb, so it doesn’t take the continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘know’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Have known’ is present perfect. This is a finished moment in the past: ‘knew’.
questions.explain: State verbs like know use the past simple.

questions.text: We        hot chocolate in the café when a famous actor walked in.
wrongReasons: ‘Drank’ is past simple. The drinking was already in progress when the actor walked in.
Wrong tense: ‘are drinking’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘we’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
questions.explain: The long action in progress is past continuous; ‘walked in’ interrupts it.

questions.text: At eleven o’clock yesterday morning, the sun        and the beach was full of people.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘the sun’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘shone’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘is shining’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: The sun was already shining at a specific past time (eleven o’clock yesterday morning).

questions.text: Lisa        TV when her mum came in, so she turned it off.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘watched’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘is watching’ is present, but this happened in the past.
Was/were mistake: ‘Lisa’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
questions.explain: The TV watching was in progress when her mum came in.

questions.text: When the teacher came back, she saw that the children        quietly.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘the children’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
Wrong tense: ‘worked’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘work’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: The children’s work was in progress when the teacher saw them.

questions.text: I        the stairs with two heavy bags when my phone rang.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘I’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘climbed’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘am climbing’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: The longer action (climbing) was in progress; ‘rang’ is the short action that interrupts it.

questions.text: At eleven last night it        heavily, so we took a taxi home from the party.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘it’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘rained’ is past simple. The action was already in progress, so use the past continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘is raining’ is present, but this happened in the past.
questions.explain: The rain was already falling at a specific past time (eleven last night).

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: ‘My friends (they)’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
After was/were the verb takes -ing: cooking, not ‘cook’.
‘The birds (they)’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘We’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘Know’ is a state verb, so it doesn’t take the continuous: Tom knew all the answers.
Double the final consonant: run → running.
‘He’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
‘He’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
‘You’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
After was/were the verb takes -ing: barking, not ‘bark’.
Double the final consonant: stop → stopping.
‘Like’ is a state verb, so it doesn’t take the continuous: I liked that song.
‘Are’ is present, but ‘last night’ is in the past: were watching.
The past continuous uses was/were, not ‘be’: he was setting.
‘They’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘She’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’: Why was she crying…?
‘You’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
After was/were the verb takes -ing: riding, not ‘ride’.
After was/were the verb takes -ing: crying, not ‘cry’.
‘My parents (they)’ takes ‘weren’t’, not ‘wasn’t’.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, -ing spelling, multiple choice, and spot-the-mistake. In the typing questions write was/were + -ing (wasn’t/weren’t in negatives; include the subject in questions). One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: At noon yesterday, Mia {{blank}} a letter to her gran.
items.explain: An action in progress at a specific past time. Drop the -e: write → writing.

items.sentText: We {{blank}} on the beach when the storm came.
items.explain: The sitting was in progress when the storm came. Double the consonant: sit → sitting.
items.wrongNote: Double the final consonant: sit → sitting.

items.sentText: I {{blank}} when you called — I was just resting.
{{blank}} at the bus stop when I drove past?
items.explain: Questions put was/were first: Were you standing…?

items.text: The kids {{blank}} in the pool when it started to rain.
wrongReasons: Spelling: ‘swiming’ is wrong — double the final m: swimming.
Was/were mistake: ‘the kids’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
Wrong tense: ‘are swimming’ is present, but this happened in the past.
items.explain: Double the final consonant: swim → swimming.

items.text: She {{blank}} a message when the bus stopped.
wrongReasons: Spelling: ‘writeing’ is wrong — drop the e: writing.
Was/were mistake: ‘she’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘is writing’ is present, but this happened in the past.

items.text: He {{blank}} up the stairs when he fell.
wrongReasons: Spelling: ‘runing’ is wrong — double the n: running.
Was/were mistake: ‘he’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘is running’ is present, but this happened in the past.
items.explain: Double the final consonant: run → running.

items.text: We {{blank}} a surprise party for Mum when she came home early.
wrongReasons: Spelling: ‘planing’ is wrong — double the n: planning.
Was/were mistake: ‘we’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
Wrong tense: ‘are planning’ is present, but this happened in the past.
items.explain: Double the final consonant: plan → planning.

items.text: Last Sunday my cousin and I {{blank}} cleaning the garage.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘my cousin and I (we)’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘Have been’ + -ing is present perfect continuous, but ‘last Sunday’ is a finished past time: ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘are’ is present, but this happened in the past.
items.explain: ‘My cousin and I’ = we, so use ‘were’.

items.text: I {{blank}} the news when the power went off.
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘I’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Wrong tense: ‘am watching’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Have watched’ is present perfect, but the power went off at a finished past moment: ‘was watching’.
items.explain: The news was in progress when the power went off.

items.text: {{blank}} you listening when she gave the instructions?
wrongReasons: Was/were mistake: ‘you’ takes ‘Were’, not ‘Was’.
Wrong tense: ‘Are’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Is’ is present and goes with he/she/it. Here it’s past and the subject is ‘you’: ‘Were’.

items.text: Mia {{blank}} the answer, so she didn’t need help.
wrongReasons: ‘Know’ is a state verb, so it doesn’t take the continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘knows’ is present, but this happened in the past.
‘Has known’ is present perfect. This is a finished moment in the past: ‘knew’.
items.explain: State verbs like know use the past simple.

items.message: ‘The cats (they)’ takes ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘I’ takes ‘was’, not ‘were’.
Drop the -e before -ing: have → having.
‘Want’ is a state verb, so it doesn’t take the continuous: He wanted a coffee.
